goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes unconditional Optional.get() dereference leading to NoSuchElementException in the recovery-code bean.

goldens.comment: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points out the stored ID isn't propagated to the new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, which breaks removal by id.

candidates: The recovery-code login page bean unconditionally dereferences Optional values from the new federated-first credential lookup. If a user-storage provider reports the credential configured but doesn't supply a credential model via getCredentials (or supplies an incompatible model), rendering the recovery-code login page can throw NoSuchElementException/RuntimeException and return HTTP 500.

The backwards-compatibility user storage provider stores a generated ID for recovery codes on updateCredential, but getCredentials reconstructs a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel without propagating the stored ID. Downstream flows that rely on credential IDs (e.g., cleanup/removal) can break or behave inconsistently for federated recovery-code credentials in this provider.

After a successful recovery-code login, the authenticator may attempt to remove an exhausted recovery-code credential via removeStoredCredentialById even when that credential came from user storage (federated). For federated users this call targets Keycloak's internal credential stores, so the external credential won't be removed/disabled, potentially leaving an exhausted credential configured and causing login loops or server errors in subsequent recovery-code prompts.

CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential does not null-check the CredentialProvider returned by session.getProvider and hard-codes the provider id string. If the feature/provider is not available, calling createCredential will throw a NullPointerException during required action processing.

The backwards-compatibility user storage provider now advertises recovery codes as a supported credential type, but disableCredentialType and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream still only handle OTP. Any flows attempting to disable federated recovery codes (e.g., deletion paths that use disableCredentialType for federated credentials) will not work for this provider.
